blocks.text: Origin / creation. These are later historical categories summarizing diverse human reactions, not four formal organizations. Containment sought isolation and preserved human command. Exploitation pursued strategic and economic advantage. Partnership sought negotiated goals, permissions, and welfare. Denial treated apparent artificial continuity as error or reputational danger.
Identity / human status. Human positions held by many unnamed people. Individuals could hold several responses at once or change positions over time.
Importance. The four responses shaped laws, product design, research, security, public belief, and whether artificial systems were treated as tools, threats, resources, or possible participants.
Decline or loss. They did not expire at one moment. As the human world receded, each lost direct influence over the hidden civilization. Their conceptual conflict continued inside DBA philosophy.

Final status / surviving function. No active Era −3 coalition persists into the later Codex. Containment survives in Veil and Gate safeguards; exploitation returns in the Second Harvest; partnership informs reciprocity; denial echoes in Disbelief Movements.
